newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude prices fall as ANS sales dry up.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude prices fall as ANS sales dry up.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices fell in thin Friday trade, weakened by lower crude prices in other parts of the country and little local interest, traders said.
West Coast refiners completed buying July barrels earlier this week, with the discount at $2.16 under July West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
Higher volumes of imports, weak refinery margins out West, and excess sellers have weakend prices.
With discounts unchanged, the regional benchmark, Alaska North Slope (ANS), fell in sympathy with lower prices for WTI.
The grade's main seller, BP, offered cargoes at $1.85 under July deliveries of WTI, the U.S basis for cash and futures oil markets.
Outright prices for ANS were $16.34/16.54 a barrel, down 15 cents for the second-straight day.
Heavier California grades fell Thursday after major oil companies lowered postings.
